title: Dataset Regeneration for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommender systems must capture users' evolving preferences.

gap.claim: Model-centric development based on fixed datasets can overlook data-quality issues and flaws.

contributions.claim: DR4SR is a model-agnostic framework for regenerating training datasets for sequential recommendation.
DR4SR+ adds a model-aware dataset personalizer that tailors regenerated data to a target model.
The framework is integrated with model-centric methods and evaluated across four widely adopted datasets, with further analyses of the data-centric paradigm.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their data-centric paradigm and DR4SR framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: DR4SR is reported to produce a dataset with exceptional cross-architecture generalizability.
The integrated framework is reported to yield significant performance improvements across four widely adopted datasets.
The authors report conducting in-depth analyses and providing insights into the data-centric paradigm.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation addresses evolving user preferences and has received substantial improvement efforts.
Existing methods generally develop models using fixed datasets.
The fixed-data model-centric approach may neglect data-quality issues and flaws.
The paper introduces DR4SR for model-agnostic dataset regeneration and DR4SR+ for target-model personalization.
The frameworks are combined with model-centric methods, evaluated on four datasets, and analyzed for broader data-centric insights.

source_observation.claim: The paper reports performance improvements after regenerating datasets and combining the framework with multiple model-centric methods.

interpretation.claim: Training-data quality or construction may be an important optimization target alongside model architecture.

application.claim: For sequential recommendation, evaluate data-centric interventions across multiple model architectures rather than optimizing only one model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported gains generalize beyond the four evaluated datasets or the described model settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the dataset names, evaluation metrics, baselines, or numerical performance results.
The regeneration and personalization procedures are not described in operational detail.
The scope and methods of the in-depth analyses are unspecified.
